Join the LKQ Family! We're looking for motivated individuals to join our team at LKQ Corporation. With opportunities for growth, competitive benefits, and a supportive work environment, LKQ is the place to be. Apply now and take the first step toward a rewarding career!

Join Our Team!

Starting Pay $24.00

The Automotive Dismantler plays a critical role in ensuring a positive customer experience. We pride ourselves on providing our customers with a quality part as described. The Yard Dismantler is responsible for properly removing all high-quality auto parts and usable core parts in a safe, efficient, and proper manner. We are seeking a highly motivated individual who must work in a fast-paced environment, is hardworking, and who can successfully meet production quotas. You must be able to multitask, communicate well with others, have hands-on automotive repair experience with a knowledge of automobiles. If you like growth and working with happy, enthusiastic individuals, you'll enjoy a career with us!

Why choose LKQ as your employer?

• Sustainable company with a great work environment,
• Full benefits coverage and pension plan available after 3 months,
• Permanent full-time position, Monday to Friday,
• Employee Parts Purchasing Program and several others benefits, and
• Recognition program with possibility of growing within the company.

What does a day look like for a Dismantler?

• Remove requested parts to fulfill orders on vehicles within the suggested time constraints in a safety conscious manner,
• Individual will be primarily responsible for dismantling drivetrain assemblies into components after assemblies have been removed from the vehicle.
• Label and tag each part to be placed in stock,
• Check the quality and product type of the inventoried parts,
• Participate in daily team goals, and
• Other duties as assigned.

What is the profile we are looking for?

• Knowledge of automotive parts,
• Diploma in mechanics or bodywork (Strong Asset!),
• Hands-on job experience,
• Ability to work in a team,
• Must be able to lift 50lbs without restrictions, and
• Must own and maintain all the tools necessary.

Job Requirements

Essential Physical Demands/Work Environment: Sits, stands, bends, lifts, and moves intermittently during working hours. Is subject to frequent interruptions. Is subject to intense physical labour, repetitive lifting. Must be able to lift at least 50-75 lbs.

Working Conditions: Employees are regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts and occasionally exposed to extreme cold & extreme heat. The noise level is moderately loud.

Take on the challenge and don't wait any longer! Apply now!

LKQ Canada is an inclusive and accessible employer, committed to an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment & selection process, and a workplace that embraces diversity & inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, including women, Indigenous peoples, visible minorities, persons with disabilities, veterans, newcomers & members of sexual minority groups. LKQ will work with applicants requesting accommodation during the hiring process.

Job Types: Full-time, Permanent

Join us for an exciting career journey with positive, driven individuals.

About this role

Overview

Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP), a standalone division of BlackRock, is a leading global infrastructure investor focused on acquiring, owning, and operating large-scale assets across the energy, transport, digital infrastructure, and water and waste management sectors.

GIP combines deep sector expertise, rigorous financial analysis, and operational capabilities to support the performance of its portfolio companies.

Key Responsibilities:

• Support the quarterly equity valuation process for a diverse global infrastructure portfolio across energy, transport, digital infrastructure, water, and waste management sectors
• Prepare valuation analyses utilizing Discounted Cash Flow (DCF), Market Multiple, and Precedent Transaction methodologies
• Assist in the development of materials for Valuation Committee meetings and senior management reporting
• Perform independent reviews of valuation assumptions, market inputs, operating performance metrics, and discount rates, including CAPM-based analyses
• Review and validate financial models to ensure consistency, accuracy, and adherence to valuation policies
• Partner closely with investment professionals, operational finance teams, fund finance teams, and portfolio company stakeholders to gather and assess key valuation inputs
• Maintain and enhance portfolio valuation databases and KPI reporting infrastructure
• Leverage technology platforms including Chronograph, Anaplan, Workiva (Wdesk), and Power BI to improve reporting, analytics, and valuation workflows
• Contribute to ongoing process improvement initiatives designed to increase efficiency, transparency, and analytical rigor across valuation activities
• Support strategic and ad hoc projects as required

Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Financial Engineering or Accounting
• Minimum of 3-5 years of experience
• Comfortable with database usage, management, and administration
• Previous experience in building and reviewing valuation models with income and market approaches

Knowledge & Skills:

• A positive attitude, high motivation and ability to maintain a culture that is based on teamwork, respect & integrity
• Resilient self-starter with ability to work independently
• Expertise with MS Excel and highly skilled with other MS office products including PowerPoint
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills
• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate effectively and credibly at executive level
• An inquisitive intellect with a strong analytical bias

For New York, NY Only the salary range for this position is USD$0.00 - USD$0.00 . Additionally, employees are eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, and benefits including healthcare, leave benefits, and retirement benefits. BlackRock operates a pay-for-performance compensation philosophy and your total compensation may vary based on role, location, and firm, department and individual performance.

Our benefits

To help you stay energized, engaged and inspired, we offer a wide range of benefits including a strong retirement plan, tuition reimbursement, comprehensive healthcare, support for working parents and Flexible Time Off (FTO) so you can relax, recharge and be there for the people you care about.

Our hybrid work model

BlackRock’s hybrid work model is designed to enable a culture of collaboration and apprenticeship that enriches the experience of our employees, while supporting flexibility for all. Employees are currently required to work at least 4 days in the office per week, with the flexibility to work from home 1 day a week. Some business groups may require more time in the office due to their roles and responsibilities. We remain focused on increasing the impactful moments that arise when we work together in person – aligned with our commitment to performance and innovation. As a new joiner, you can count on this hybrid model to accelerate your learning and onboarding experience here at BlackRock.

Guidance on AI use for candidates

At BlackRock, AI has long been part of how we work – enhancing decision-making, improving operations, and helping us deliver better outcomes for clients. We encourage candidates to use AI thoughtfully to learn, prepare, and work more effectively; but during our interview process, we want to focus on getting to know you through your own experiences, thinking, and judgment. To support you, we’ve provided guidance on when and how to use AI during our hiring process so you can approach each step with confidence and showcase your best self.

About BlackRock

At BlackRock, we are all connected by one mission: to help more and more people experience financial well-being. Our clients, and the people they serve, are saving for retirement, paying for their children’s educations, buying homes and starting businesses. Their investments also help to strengthen the global economy: support businesses small and large; finance infrastructure projects that connect and power cities; and facilitate innovations that drive progress.

This mission would not be possible without our smartest investment – the one we make in our employees. It’s why we’re dedicated to creating an environment where our colleagues feel welcomed, valued and supported with networks, benefits and development opportunities to help them thrive.

To learn more about BlackRock, please visit Careers.BlackRock.com. We also encourage you to get to know us on LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube, X, and TikTok.

THE ASSOCIATE ROLE

The Associate is the operational lead on LAS engagements and a genuine thought partner in the advisory process. Associates transform leadership data into business-relevant insights: identifying patterns in people and teams, determining what those patterns mean for organizational outcomes, and communicating those implications in ways that help clients make better talent decisions.

Associates own workstreams end-to-end. They drive the project plan, conduct and support interviews and assessments, synthesize qualitative and quantitative data, write the reports and client materials, and keep engagements moving. They partner closely with Consultants, who own the client relationship and the final deliverable, while taking real accountability for quality, pace, and the client experience along the way.

This is a role with meaningful ownership. It is also a support role in an apprenticeship model: Associates build credibility, judgment, and client exposure over time, and responsibility grows as that credibility is earned.

WHAT YOU WILL ACTUALLY DO

The work varies by Solution and by team, but the following responsibilities are consistent across the role.

Insight development and client deliverables

• Synthesize qualitative and quantitative data from interviews, assessments, diagnostics, and secondary research to identify themes, insights, and implications

• Write and own client deliverables, Advanced Leadership Profile (ALP) and Leadership Profile (LP) assessment reports, group and comparison reports, culture and team diagnostic outputs, board materials, workshop decks, and executive summaries

• Draft assessment components independently, including Individual Style Profile (ISP), 360, capabilities, strengths and development opportunities, and summary pages; over time, contribute Executive Intelligence (ExI) insights

• Connect leadership insight to business context, company performance, value creation, role requirements, and the risks and opportunities facing the client

Assessment, interviews, and client interaction

• Conduct and support executive and stakeholder interviews; lead, co-lead, or participate in assessments depending on the Solution, the engagement, and the Consultant

• Conduct 360 reference interviews and synthesize input into balanced, evidence-based summaries

• Lead internal calibration calls and contribute an informed, data-backed point of view on scoring and conclusions

• Participate in client debriefs, workshops, and readouts; over time, debrief participants and lead segments of client sessions

• Administer proprietary leadership advisory tools and diagnostics (ISP, culture, team effectiveness, and related instruments) in partnership with the Consultant, and analyze the resulting data

• Represent the Firm with professionalism, maturity, and poise in written, verbal, virtual, and in-person settings, and handle confidential information with discretion

Engagement and project management

• Own the project plan and timeline end-to-end; organize and facilitate team touchpoints, including kick-offs, check-ins, and project recaps

• Serve as a day-to-day point of contact for the client alongside the Consultant, and draft client and stakeholder communications

• Organize and distribute work across the engagement team, clarify roles, and hold the team accountable to deadlines

• Anticipate what the client, Consultant, and team will need next; identify risks early, escalate appropriately, and propose a path forward

• Synthesize client meetings, board interactions, and workshops into clear themes, decisions, and next steps

• Manage several engagements at once across time zones and competing deadlines, and maintain your capacity tracker accurately so staffing decisions can be made well

• Use AI-enabled tools thoughtfully to improve efficiency in research, drafting, and summarization, always validating sources and conclusions, exercising judgment around client data and confidentiality, and retaining human accountability for the insight

Developing others and building the practice

• Guide Analysts on first-draft documents, provide examples and standards, and give timely, constructive feedback

• Serve as an onboarding or apprenticeship mentor to new colleagues and contribute to their integration

• Contribute to Solution and intellectual capital development, case studies, best practices, and internal tools

• Build relationships with Executive Search colleagues and help them understand where LAS can add value for their clients

• Occasionally support business development, contributing to qualifications decks, proposal materials, and background research. Associates are rarely involved in client pitches; that exposure typically comes at the Senior Associate level and beyond.

YOUR FIRST YEAR

We invest heavily in structured onboarding, and we expect training to take priority over client work in the early months. New Associates are not expected to take a project solo until they have demonstrated proficiency in that skill under the mentorship of an experienced colleague.

A typical first-year path includes:

• Firm and LAS onboarding — understanding our business model, strategy, services, and how Search and LAS work together.

• Core curriculum — Insight Foundations, Insight Bootcamp, Overview of Capabilities, Culture in Action, the Leadership Model, the 360s course, Writing with Impact, and ExI Bootcamp.

• Assessment — shadow full ALPs; lead 360 interviews and write the page solo; write ISP and capabilities pages; write strengths, development opportunities, and summary pages; build toward delivering a full ALP report at roughly 80 percent client readiness.

• Organizational consulting — administer and analyze ISP, culture, and team effectiveness surveys; draft group and culture reports; debrief the culture graph; support workshop design, materials, and onsite coordination.

• Business acumen — how businesses make money, different operating and ownership models, organizational structures, C-suite roles and responsibilities, and basic financial literacy. This is supported by the LAS Business Acumen Series (Business Strategy, Financial Basics, Anatomy of a Company, Engagement and Client Management).

• Consulting skills — craft a credible introduction for clients, present informed opinions and defend them with data, professionally challenge the views of others, and proactively seek feedback from every project team.

THE SUPPORT AROUND YOU

You will not be left to figure this out alone. Every new Associate is supported by a defined team:

• Talent Partner — your manager, responsible for your development, staffing, and performance, with a recurring one-on-one cadence

• Onboarding mentor — a peer who helps you navigate the Firm, its systems, and its unwritten rules

• Apprenticeship mentors — one to two Associates or Senior Associates who are your first point of contact for client work; new hires are paired with a dedicated Consultant or Senior Associate capacity for the first six to twelve months, so you learn by apprenticeship

• Engagement teams — Consultants, Associates, and Executive Engagement Assistants who coach you in the flow of the work

• The AAPM community — the Associate & Analyst Practice Member group, which runs monthly calls, coffee chats, learning cafés, and peer development programming

THE REALITIES OF THE ROLE

We would rather be direct than have you discover these after you join.

• The workload is deadline-driven and uneven. Priorities are set by client needs and Consultant schedules. There are genuinely intense stretches around report deadlines, board readouts, and workshops, and quieter stretches in between. This is client service: timelines shift, clients reschedule, and there will be occasional work outside normal hours to meet a client commitment.

• Assessment work is rigorous. Spending several hours on camera with a participant and then multiple hours writing and nuancing a report is demanding. It is also core to what we do. We balance assessment with other work to give you a variety.

• Staffing is partially relationship-based. Opportunities are influenced by the connections, trust, and internal reputation you build. Early on, you will work on what the practice needs, which may not always be the work that energizes you most. Over time, you gain far more influence over the projects and people you work with, but you have to invest in the relationships to get there.

• The work is predominantly at the most senior levels. Because we work with C-suite executives and boards, there are fewer opportunities to independently lead assessments early on than at firms that work deeper in the organization. This also leads to what makes the role great (below).

• Autonomy can feel like ambiguity. You will be trusted to manage your own time and to choose work in partnership with your Talent Partner. Not every step will be laid out for you.

• The learning curve is real. Our methodology is complex, and our quality bar is high. Most Associates, including those with directly relevant prior experience, need several months before they feel confident with the tools, frameworks, and standards. That is expected.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE WORTH IT

• Exposure to senior leaders and consequential decisions. Associates work directly on material that reaches C-suite executives, boards, and investors, and contributes to decisions that shape organizations. That exposure typically comes much later in a career elsewhere.

• Accelerated learning. You will see how successful leaders think, make decisions, and navigate complexity across many companies, industries, and situations in a fraction of the time it would take from inside a single organization.

• Exceptional colleagues. Our people are consistently named as the best part of working here: smart, generous with their time, deeply committed to quality, and invested in helping one another improve.

• Quality over volume. We prioritize thoughtful analysis, sound judgment, and exceptional work products over speed or scale. That creates a steeper learning curve and a far better development experience.

• Variety and breadth. Public and private companies across every major sector, and work spanning assessment, succession, culture, team effectiveness, development, and organizational effectiveness.

• Real ownership. You own workstreams, deliverables and client communications, and you have meaningful influence over your schedule, your projects and your career path.

• A developmental culture. Structured curriculum, apprenticeship mentoring, real-time feedback on every project, a published development framework and colleagues who are invested in your growth rather than competing with you.

KEY RELATIONSHIPS

Reports to

Talent Partner (Leadership Advisory Services)

Day-to-day direction

Consultants and Senior Associates, on a per-engagement basis

Career guidance

Counselor (Consultant), onboarding mentor and apprenticeship mentors

Other key relationships

Analysts; Project Managers; Executive Engagement Assistants; Content Editors; Client Care Liaisons; Knowledge Management and Solution Support; Executive Search colleagues; the Associate & Analyst Practice Member (AAPM) community

Location

Based in one of our North American offices

CANDIDATE PROFILE

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

• Generally four or more years of relevant professional experience in leadership advisory, executive assessment, management or strategy consulting, organizational development, human capital or talent management, or a relevant industry role.

• Undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. An advanced degree (for example, in organizational psychology, industrial-organizational psychology, business or a related field) is helpful but not required; relevant professional experience can substitute.

• Superior business writing skills, evidenced through project work or a writing sample provided on request

• Demonstrated ability to synthesize complex qualitative and quantitative information into clear, evidence-based insight

• Strong project management and organizational skills, with a track record of managing multiple priorities and competing deadlines

• General business acumen developed through exposure to a range of business situations and contexts

• Executive presence and interpersonal effectiveness; comfort interacting with senior leaders

• Client deliverables are written in English; superior English business writing is an essential function of the role. Additional languages are an advantage.

• Work authorization for the country in which you are applying

WHO TENDS TO THRIVE HERE

• Intellectually curious people who want to understand the “why” behind people, businesses, and organizational outcomes, and who enjoy connecting disparate pieces of information into a point of view

• People who combine intellectual confidence with genuine humility, and who engage readily with feedback and iteration

• Strong writers and communicators who take visible pride in the quality of their work and the accuracy of their details

• Self-directed people who are comfortable creating structure where none exists, figuring things out independently, and taking ownership of their own career

• Resourceful relationship builders who proactively reach out, build trust across teams, and adapt their style to different personalities and Consultant preferences

• People who are comfortable with ambiguity, shifting priorities, and the pace of client service

• Team-oriented colleagues with a “no task too small” mindset who contribute beyond their immediate responsibilities

• People with poise, maturity, and professional presence

IS THIS ROLE RIGHT FOR YOU?

We would rather you have a clear picture now than discover it after you join. The role consistently requires the following. If these conditions do not match what you are looking for, this may not be the right fit:

• Earned scope rather than immediate ownership. Client relationship ownership and independent assessment leadership expand as demonstrated quality and trust are established, not from day one.

• Working without a defined process. Engagements vary by Solution, client, and Consultant. The role requires building your own structure, workflows, and standards in the absence of fixed procedures.

• Extensive writing and multiple revision cycles. Writing is an essential function. Deliverables routinely undergo several rounds of substantive feedback and rework before reaching the client.

• Owning your own project management. The role carries end-to-end accountability for timelines, coordination, and follow-up. Dedicated project management support is not provided.

• Building internal relationships that influence staffing. Engagement assignments are shaped in part by internal trust and reputation, which the role requires you to actively develop.

• Capability-based advancement. Progression to Consultant is assessed against a published framework and takes time; it is not tenure-driven or accelerated on request.

• Limited early opportunity to independently lead assessments. Because our work sits at the C-suite and board level, independent assessment leadership comes later than at firms working deeper in the organization.

• Influence through partnership rather than sole authority. Decisions are reached collaboratively with Consultants and engagement teams.

• A distinct business from Executive Search. LAS has different client work, methodologies, and career paths.

CRITICAL CAPABILITIES FOR SUCCESS

These capabilities form the basis of the LAS Associate Development Framework and of the assessment of performance and promotion readiness. We share them openly so you know what you are signing up for and how you will be evaluated.

Project management

Manages overall projects and oversees the team's collective efforts to drive the cadence and flow of client outcomes.

• Owns the project workplan across multiple workstreams; organizes and facilitates team touchpoints and keeps the team accountable

• Takes ownership of whole projects and serves as a day-to-day point of contact with the client

• Manages multiple engagements with competing deadlines; sets expectations, clarifies roles, and avoids duplication of effort

• Anticipates challenges, adjusts priorities, and pushes back internally as appropriate

• Remains calm under pressure and delivers on commitments, or raises slippage early with a proposed solution

• Uses technology and AI-enabled tools to improve project efficiency, with appropriate validation

Client insights

Gathers nuanced insight from sophisticated data collection and delivers it in a way that is relevant for clients and resonates with participants.

• Co-administers our tools and develops independent insights under the supervision of a Consultant or more experienced colleague; knows how each tool relates to the others and to our overall methodology

• Elevates perspective to discern themes across individuals and deliver nuanced insight at the team or organizational level

• Highlights and resolves inconsistencies or contradictions in the data to reach a more nuanced narrative

• Produces client-ready documents, assessment reports, comparison reports, and board decks with limited assistance

• Conveys insight compellingly, beyond “just the facts,” tailored to the audience and the client situation

• Engages in constructive discussion with the Consultant, defending a view and amending it when the evidence warrants

Impact and effectiveness

Communicates effectively in writing and verbally; has executive presence and builds trusted relationships.

• Establishes productive relationships with clients, participants, and colleagues across the Firm, and builds a personal brand defined by reliability and collaboration

• Adapts style to the audience, coaching with participants, business-insight-driven with clients, and remains composed under pressure

• Contributes meaningfully in debriefs, assessments, workshops, and client conversations without being prompted

• Coordinates team efforts on complex projects; unblocks obstacles and helps create consensus

• Places team goals ahead of individual goals; volunteers to share workload and shares information generously while being rigorous about confidentiality

Business and market knowledge

Obtains and incorporates knowledge across one or more of our Solutions to enhance client work in a meaningful way.

• Builds deep knowledge of the concepts and principles underlying our assessment, culture, team, development, succession, and performance acceleration frameworks, and can teach others

• Develops foundational business acumen, financial statements, executive role responsibilities, organizational structures, and operating models, and applies them to the client context

• Shows curiosity about the bigger picture surrounding an assignment, taking a systems view that considers company and industry context

• Understands how Search and LAS work together, and navigates internal resources, materials, and experts to bring the best of the Firm to client work

• Stays current on business, economic, and leadership advisory news, and brings relevant insight to teams and clients

Developing self and others

Seeks and provides feedback; coaches and mentors to improve team performance; modifies own performance based on input.

• Proactively seeks feedback from every project team and demonstrates progress against development areas over time

• Takes personal responsibility for career development, engaging mentors and sponsors, and articulating aspirations clearly

• Provides balanced, behavioral feedback to junior colleagues and creates opportunities for their development

• Serves as an onboarding or apprenticeship mentor and supports the integration of new colleagues

Firm values

Champions the Firm's values, culture, and Code of Conduct; engages, participates, and collaborates with others.

• Demonstrates alignment to Firm values in everyday behavior; is professional, cordial, and engaging in all settings

• Brings cultural awareness and sensitivity to every interaction with colleagues and clients

• Participates actively in office, practice, and Firm-wide activities, and builds a network beyond LAS

• Leverages AI responsibly, maintaining human accountability for client data, confidential information, and intellectual property

• Represents Spencer Stuart well and lives by the Code of Conduct

Career path and progression

Level: Associate

What changes: Own workstreams end-to-end; manage substantial project components with increasing autonomy; build trusted client relationships; synthesize data into clear, client-relevant insight; create structure from ambiguity; begin developing others intentionally.

Typical review cadence: Entry point

Level: Senior Associate

What changes: Lead client interactions and complex, multi-Solution programs; deepen advisory expertise; progress toward Associate Consultant and Consultant roles or to other internal opportunities across the Firm.

Typical review cadence: Reviewed twice per year

Level: Associate Consultant and beyond

What changes: Advise clients in the first seat; develop distinctive Solution or industry expertise; support and originate commercial opportunities; progress toward the Consultant and Partner track or to other senior opportunities across the Firm.

Typical review cadence: Reviewed annually

Review cadence is typical, not guaranteed; promotion is capability-based and discretionary. Associates also pursue a range of paths beyond the LAS delivery track, including roles elsewhere in the Firm.

HOW WE WORK

• Hybrid working. Colleagues are in the office a minimum of two days per week. For new hires, we strongly recommend three to four days per week during the early months, because learning, shadowing, and relationship-building happen fastest in person. Best practice is to choose the days your team is also in. Subject to reasonable accommodation.

• Staffing and autonomy. New Associates are paired with one to two Consultants or Senior Associates for their first six to twelve months. As your network develops, you take a greater role in choosing projects in partnership with your Talent Partner, weighing interests, developmental value, relationships, and goals.

• Travel. Travel is modest and has decreased as assessments have moved largely online. Expect roughly 25-50 percent at the high end, primarily for client workshops, onsite sessions, occasional board meetings, and Firm events, with considerable variation by Solution and team. Most associates travel less than 20% of their time.

• Flexibility. We are a client-service business. Timelines shift, and there will be occasional early, late or rescheduled work to meet a client commitment. In exchange, you have real control over how you manage the rest of your time.

The base compensation range for this position is $100,000 –150,000 per year. The actual base compensation within the range above will be dependent on the individual’s skills, experiences, and qualifications. This position may be eligible to participate in our annual discretionary bonus program.

Spencer Stuart also offers a competitive benefits package, which includes:

• Retirement savings plan with discretionary profit sharing contribution and employer match;
• PTO (minimum 15 days per year, increases with tenure), paid sick time (10 days per year), company holidays (12 days per year), and paid leaves of absence when applicable;
• Comprehensive health benefits, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, and healthcare flexible spending account;
• Life Insurance, and short-term and long-term disability insurance;
• Wellness benefits, including an employee assistance program, virtual mental health program, and mindfulness program; and
• Voluntary benefit options, including supplemental life insurance, identity theft protection, and whole life insurance with long-term care and critical illness coverage.

Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and plan terms and may change.

You'll direct AI output at volume, both across Lovable’s brand and creative and Lovable’s output itself. You’ll be working closely with a Brand Engineer to ensure whatever workflow you wish for can scale. This is a new role with no precedent - you’ll be defining a lot of it as you go.

Why Lovable?

Lovable is the software creation platform that gives people the power to act on the problems closest to them. For decades, turning an idea into software required so much capital, technical fluency, and time that many ideas never came to life. Lovable is the counterargument: a platform for all people with ideas, ambition, and problems worth solving. From solopreneurs to small business owners to teams at companies like Adidas and Zendesk, people have built over 60 million projects on Lovable since its launch in November 2024. And we’re just getting started.

We’re building a generational company from Stockholm, with growing teams in London, Boston, New York, and San Francisco. Our team is small, talent-dense, and moving quickly, with a culture rooted in extreme ownership, high velocity, and low-ego collaboration. We look for people who care deeply, ship fast, and are eager to make a dent in the world.

Lovable is one of TIME’s 100 Most Influential Companies and has been recognized on the Forbes AI 50 and CNBC Disruptor 50, reflecting our momentum as one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies and one of the most ambitious places to build in this next era of software.

What we're looking for

- Strong design taste - you can tell good from generic, and you can articulate why

- Real fluency with AI generation tools (image, video, whatever's next) as a craft, not a party trick - you already have opinions about which models and workflows produce better output and why

- Experience creating scalable brand systems, templates, tools, and guidelines that enable teams to execute independently - except here the "team" increasingly includes the AI pipeline itself

- A portfolio of shipped brand assets - campaign visuals, social graphics, presentation decks, event materials, marketing collateral - plus evidence of AI-native production, not just AI-assisted

- Comfortable with ambiguity - this function doesn't have a template at Lovable or anywhere else yet

- Technical range - prompt engineering counts, scripting, automation and building custom tools is even better. We're not asking you to be an engineer, but the more range you have the faster the seam between you and the Brand Engineer disappears.

What you'll do

How we hire

1. Fill in a short form then jump on an initial exploratory call.

3. Join us for a round of interviews to discuss your experience in more depth

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

We are seeking an Enterprise Account Executive, Industries - BFSI to pioneer Anthropic's enterprise AI adoption across India's banking, financial services, and insurance sector. You will build our presence from the ground up, securing transformative deals with leading banks, NBFCs, insurers, and fintechs, and establishing Anthropic as their trusted AI partner for digital transformation. You will navigate the complex, regulated environment of Indian financial institutions and position Claude as the AI solution that drives both efficiency and innovation while maintaining the highest standards of safety and reliability. As one of our first industry specialists in India, you will shape our BFSI go-to-market strategy and build the playbook for how Anthropic serves financial institutions, working closely with global teams while adapting our approach to local market dynamics. This position is based in Bangalore, Mumbai, or NCR, with travel across India.

Key responsibilities

• Establish Anthropic's enterprise presence across India's BFSI sector, including public and private sector banks, NBFCs, insurers, asset managers, and fintechs
• Develop BFSI-specific strategies that account for RBI, IRDAI, and SEBI requirements, data localization needs, and sector compliance standards
• Build relationships with key stakeholders, including CXOs, Chief Risk and Compliance Officers, digital transformation leaders, and innovation heads at India's top financial institutions
• Create the India BFSI playbook for enterprise AI adoption, documenting successful approaches that can scale across the region
• Own end-to-end sales cycles for complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise deals, often involving board-level decisions
• Drive strategic expansion within lighthouse accounts that can serve as references for the entire BFSI industry
• Navigate procurement processes unique to Indian financial institutions, including vendor risk assessments, rate contracts, empanelment procedures, and multi-year agreements
• Collaborate with system integrators and consulting partners who often influence technology decisions at banks and insurers
• Co-innovate with customers to develop BFSI use cases, from vernacular customer service and fraud detection to credit underwriting and automated compliance reporting
• Understand sector-specific challenges such as financial inclusion, legacy core banking modernization, and data security in regulated environments
• Position AI strategically within the context of Digital India initiatives and financial sector modernization programs
• Ensure successful deployments that can scale from proof-of-concept to enterprise-wide implementation
• Partner with global product teams to prioritize features critical for Indian financial institutions, such as multi-language support, data residency, auditability, and integration with local systems
• Collaborate with legal and compliance teams to navigate India's evolving AI and data protection regulations
• Provide market intelligence on competitive dynamics, pricing expectations, and emerging BFSI use cases unique to India
• Build internal alignment between Anthropic's global strategy and India's market requirements

Minimum qualifications

• 15+ years of enterprise sales experience in the Indian market, with a proven track record of closing large, complex deals, ideally across BFSI sector
• Deep understanding of how Indian financial institutions operate, including decision-making processes, budget cycles, and stakeholder dynamics
• Experience selling transformational technology (Cloud, AI/ML, Digital Transformation platforms) to Indian enterprises
• Established relationships with senior executives across banks, NBFCs, insurers, or fintechs
• Understanding of the Indian regulatory landscape, including RBI, NSE, IRDAI, and SEBI requirements, data protection laws, and sector-specific compliance
• Consultative selling expertise, with the ability to position AI as a strategic business driver rather than just a technology solution
• Complex deal structuring experience, including multi-year contracts, phased deployments, and outcome-based pricing
• Technical acumen to engage credibly with CTOs, architects, and data science teams
• Cross-cultural communication skills to work effectively with both Indian stakeholders and global teams
• Entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to build a market from scratch with limited local resources initially
• Patient yet persistent approach to long enterprise sales cycles, while maintaining momentum

Preferred qualifications

• Experience selling directly into large Indian banks, insurers, or financial conglomerates
• Relationships with Indian system integrators such as TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and HCL, particularly their BFSI practices
• Familiarity with Indian business groups and conglomerates, and how decisions flow within these complex organizations
• Track record of first-in-market roles or launching new products in India
• Domain expertise in areas critical to Indian financial services, such as UPI payments, core banking systems, KYC/AML compliance, Aadhaar integration, or insurance underwriting
• Knowledge of government initiatives such as Digital India and their impact on financial sector technology adoption
• Experience navigating public sector bank and PSU sales processes is a plus

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
